x_add_helper_hint: You can add configurations now; to connect you will need the helper (Settings → Helper).
x_app_icon_body: Changes the icon in your browser's toolbar. Your configurations and any live connection are untouched.
x_build_signature: Vazie VPN extension %1$s · helper %2$s · by Vazovsky
x_clipboard_unavailable: The browser wouldn't let Vazie VPN read the clipboard. Paste the link into the field.
x_engine_failed: The engine couldn't be installed. Check your connection and try again.
x_engine_needed_body: The helper is here, but the Xray engine is not. It is downloaded once from its own release and checked against a pinned SHA-256.
x_failure_engine: The Xray engine isn't installed yet
x_failure_helper: The Vazie VPN helper isn't installed or couldn't start
x_failure_proxy: Another extension or a policy controls the browser's proxy
x_guidance_appearance_body: The theme and the toolbar icon: how Vazie VPN looks inside and in your browser.
x_guidance_guides_body: The toolbar button, the right-click menu, the side panel and notifications — how to use each.
x_guidance_split_body: Choose sites that go around the VPN, or the only sites that go through it.
x_guide_helper_summary: The small program that runs the tunnel.
x_guide_menu_body: Right-clicking the Vazie VPN button offers your recent configurations directly, and Connect or Disconnect. Nothing to set up — they are already there.
x_guide_menu_step_1: Right-click the Vazie VPN button in the toolbar.
x_guide_menu_summary: Right-click the icon and pick one — nothing to set up.
x_guide_notification_body_off: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN can show a notification with a Disconnect button, so you can stop it without opening the extension. Notifications are off right now, so it can't.
x_guide_notification_body_on: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN shows a notification with a Disconnect button, so you can stop it without opening the extension.
x_guide_notification_step_1: If you turned notifications off for the browser, allow them in your system's notification settings.
x_guide_notification_step_2: Press Allow notifications above and accept the browser's question.
x_guide_notification_summary: A notification with a Disconnect button while the tunnel is up.
x_guide_panel_body: The side panel keeps Vazie VPN open next to the page, with the same screens as the popup. The popup closes when you click away; the panel does not.
x_guide_panel_step_1: Click the toolbar button, then the gear.
x_guide_panel_step_2: Choose Open in the side panel.
x_guide_panel_step_3: Close it with the × in the panel's corner.
x_guide_panel_summary: A panel that stays open while you browse.
x_guide_toolbar_body: Pinned to the toolbar, Vazie VPN shows in its icon whether you are protected, and connects from its popup.
x_guide_toolbar_step_1: Click the puzzle-piece button in the browser's toolbar.
x_guide_toolbar_step_2: Find Vazie VPN in the list.
x_guide_toolbar_step_3: Click the pin next to it.
x_guide_toolbar_summary: One click to connect, and the state at a glance.
x_guide_toolbar_title: Pin Vazie VPN to the toolbar
x_helper_advanced_body: Run the downloaded installer from the terminal, from the folder it was downloaded to. It finds this extension in your browsers by itself; if you install the extension later, run it again.
x_helper_needed_body: A browser can't open a tunnel on its own. The helper is a small program on this computer that runs your configuration.
x_helper_remove: To remove the helper later, run vazie-vpn-host uninstall.
x_helper_s2_macos: Open the downloaded file and follow the installer. If macOS says it can't verify the developer, right-click the file and choose Open.
x_helper_s2_other: Open the downloaded file. If your system warns about an unknown publisher, choose More info → Run anyway.
x_helper_s3: Come back here. This page notices the helper by itself — nothing to press.
x_helper_unknown_os: Your system isn't one the installers are made for. Build the helper from the repository (cargo build --release in apps/native-host) and run it.
x_helper_why: A browser extension can't open a tunnel on its own: it can't run a VPN engine or listen on a port. The helper is a small program on this computer that does both, for your own configuration. The extension only tells the browser to use it.
x_link_copied: Link copied. The clipboard is cleared in 30 seconds.
x_manage_list_body: Click a configuration to use it. Point at it to delete it — deleting always asks first.
x_notification_prompt_body: While a tunnel is up, Vazie VPN can show a notification with a Disconnect button — so you can stop it without opening the extension. Vazie VPN connects either way.
x_onboarding_own_body: Vazie VPN ships with no servers, so the first thing to do is paste a VLESS link you already have. It is stored encrypted in this browser and never uploaded — not to us, not to anyone. There is no account to create and nothing to pay for. To connect, it also needs a small helper program on this computer; I'll show you where.
x_onboarding_reach_body: A toolbar button that shows the state at a glance, your configurations in its right-click menu, a keyboard shortcut and a side panel. Nothing to set up right now — I'll point out the basics in a moment.
x_onboarding_welcome_body: I look after the tunnel in this extension. I'll be on the home screen telling you whether you're protected, and I'll be sleeping when you're not. Give me thirty seconds and I'll show you around.
x_onboarding_what_body: A VPN client: it opens an encrypted tunnel between this browser and a server, so the network you are on sees traffic to that server and nothing about where it goes next. Vazie VPN is the client. It is not a service that watches over you.
x_privacy_export_body: Export produces the original share link, and that link contains the credentials that connect to the server. Anyone who receives it can use the server as you. Vazie VPN copies it to the clipboard at the moment you ask and clears the clipboard 30 seconds later.
x_privacy_helper_engine: The engine (Xray) is downloaded once from its own GitHub release, and refused unless its SHA-256 matches the one pinned in the helper.
x_privacy_helper_local: The helper runs on this computer only and opens a proxy that listens on 127.0.0.1 and nowhere else, on a new port for every connection. The configuration reaches the engine through a pipe, never through a file.
x_privacy_logs_body: Vazie VPN writes nothing to the browser console, and never writes a key, a UUID, a share link or a server address into any log. The helper starts the engine with logging off.
x_privacy_stores_configs: Your configurations: the server address, the port, the transport and security settings, and the keys needed to connect.
x_privacy_surfaces_menu: The right-click menu offers up to three configurations by name. A name that looks like an address, a link, an e-mail, an IP or a UUID is left out rather than shortened.
x_privacy_surfaces_notification: The notification, if you allow it, shows the connection state and nothing else. It never names a configuration.
x_privacy_surfaces_permissions: The extension asks the browser for access to a subscription's server only when you add that subscription, and gives it back afterwards. The one site it always talks to is the Vazie backend, for the About links and the questions.
x_privacy_surfaces_title: The toolbar, the menu and notifications
x_privacy_vpn_body: While connected, the traffic of this browser goes through the server in the configuration you chose. That server can see the destinations your browser asks for, exactly as your network provider could otherwise. Vazie VPN is the client; it does not run in between. Other programs on this computer are not tunnelled.
x_privacy_vpn_dns: Names are looked up by the server, not by your provider. While every site uses the tunnel, WebRTC is kept from showing your real address.
x_privacy_where_encrypted: Configurations and their keys are encrypted in this browser profile with a key the browser holds and no code can export. Web pages and other extensions cannot read them.
x_privacy_where_plain: Your theme, icon, sites for split tunneling and dismissed tips are in plain browser storage — they are preferences, not secrets, and keeping them apart means a display setting cannot break the store that holds your keys.
x_privacy_where_sync: Nothing is synced. Vazie VPN does not use the browser's sync storage, so your configurations never travel through your browser account.
x_proxy_other_body: Another extension or your organisation's policy controls the proxy settings, so Vazie VPN can't route this browser. Turn the other one off and try again.
x_split_empty: No sites chosen yet. With none chosen, every site uses the VPN.
x_split_mode_exclude_body: The sites you pick go straight through your provider; everything else uses the VPN.
x_split_mode_include_body: Only the sites you pick use the VPN; everything else goes straight through your provider.
x_split_mode_off_body: Every page in this browser uses the tunnel.
x_split_note: A site also covers its subdomains. Addresses on your own network (localhost, 192.168.x.x, .local) never go through the tunnel. Changes apply at once.
x_subscription_permission: Vazie VPN needs the browser's permission to ask %1$s for the list. Without it nothing is downloaded.
x_tour_done_body: Vazie VPN also has a right-click menu on its toolbar button, a keyboard shortcut and a side panel. None of it is required — the guides are there when you want them.
x_update_unavailable_body: This copy of Vazie VPN wasn't installed from a store, so there is nowhere to ask. A store updates its own copy automatically.
